entry.title: GPT-5.6 Sol improved an upper bound from a 2019 paper by Terry Tao in just 13 minutes

link.title: GPT-5.6 Sol improved an upper bound from a 2019 paper by Terry Tao in just 13 minutes

entry.content:
There is a classical result in operator theory with broad implications for quantum mechanics: the operator equation ( [D, X] = 1 ) has no exact solutions for bounded operators. What if we want to solve it approximately?

Popa proved that, for a solution with error less than ( \varepsilon ), the operators must have norm at least ( \frac{1}{2}\log(1/\varepsilon) ). However, we do not yet know whether this bound is achievable. In 2019, Tao constructed a solution with norm ( O(\log^5(1/\varepsilon)) ). Today, GPT-5.6 Sol improved this result to ( O(\log^4(1/\varepsilon)) ) in just 13 minutes, then formalized it in Lean in less than three hours.

Perhaps the biggest highlight is that both the proof and the formalization were completed with just a Plus subscription, so you do not need Pro to obtain new results already. Could Tao or anyone else do it themselves? Definitely, but it would likely take much more time: Tao himself improved the exponent from 16 to 5 following reviewer comments.

Challenge: Can Pro achieve the conjectured ( O(\log(1/\varepsilon)) ) bound?
